title: LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training
abstract: Lossless tensor compression could reduce memory usage during training, but training requires tensors to be repeatedly re-encoded. We introduce Losslessly Compressed Tensors (LCT), a GPU execution framework designed for this repeated encode-decode regime. LCT exploits the natural redundancy in floating point data to reduce storage for weights, activations and optimizer states. Highly optimized GPU kernels implement Huffman coding with precomputed codebooks for low compression and decompression overhead, essential for training. Our analysis characterizes LCT's storage costs and adaptation to magnitude shifts. LCT achieves a compression ratio of up to $1.455\times$, and is demonstrated in training and finetuning settings. On a 162M-parameter NanoGPT, LCT reduces memory usage by $24.6\%$ for a $7.2\%$ step-time increase. In Qwen3-4B fine-tuning, LCT saves up to $23.8\%$ of peak memory, enabling a $3.5\times$ larger context length in training on the same GPU.

title: Inflak: A Unified Orchestration Architecture for Human-Agent Interaction
abstract: LLM-powered agents increasingly support open-ended activities, yet orchestrating when and how agents interact with humans remains challenging. Existing approaches often provide interaction mechanisms tied to particular tasks or execution patterns, lacking a unified architecture for diverse and evolving interaction needs. We introduce Inflak, a unified four-layer architecture for human-agent interaction orchestration that separates state reconstruction and routing, interaction and execution planning, interaction design, and interface rendering. Its layered design with progressive resolution enables general applicability, runtime flexibility, module composability, and orchestration maintainability. We implement Inflak as agent-native, skill-based plugins within a general-purpose agent framework and evaluate it through a gallery of various application scenarios and interaction paradigms, technical performance testing, and a comparative implementation case study. The evaluations show that Inflak can serve as a general and extensible foundation for orchestrating diverse human-agent interaction flows.

title: From Sketch to Scene: Relightable Garment Reconstruction from Marked Sketches
abstract: Sketching is one of the most natural ways for people to express visual ideas. Unlike the text prompts that most generative systems rely on today, a sketch captures spatial structure and intent directly, including where a designer wants highlights and shadows to appear. Yet current sketch-to-3D pipelines have no input for that intent: they bake the drawn shading into the texture as dark paint, and the light cannot be moved. We propose a system that transforms a rough garment sketch, marked with sparse annotations (a star for a highlight and a moon for a shadow), and a short text prompt describing the texture, into a textured 3D mesh with an explicit directional light, as a scene that can be relit and edited after generation. The two symbols are the most frequent proposals in an elicitation study with art students. From the marked sketch the system predicts the scene's directional light and, separately, a displacement field that bends the surface so that the moon-marked regions fall into shadow under that light, rather than being painted dark in the texture.

title: AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder
abstract: Most vision-language models (VLMs) treat the vision encoder as a static feature extractor: it encodes an image once, independently of the question, and leaves subsequent reasoning to the language model. Yet different questions may require different visual operations and processing depths. We present AdaLoop, a framework for question-conditioned visual recurrence in VLMs. AdaLoop adapts visual computation to the question and reuses the encoder's transformations across multiple iterations, with the pretrained vision weights frozen. We also introduce VisRO, a procedural dataset and generation pipeline for training and evaluating vision-centric reasoning. On six VisRO tasks, AdaLoop outperforms standard fine-tuning and question-conditioned single-pass baselines with matched training data and optimizer updates. These gains hold across three VLM families on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution examples. Our findings suggest that pretrained vision encoders can contribute to reasoning through task-directed, iterative visual computation.

title: Zoetrope: A Deadline-Aware Architecture for Continuous Multimodal Perception, Reasoning, and Authorized Action
abstract: A live visual assistant must do more than describe successive images: it must maintain a coherent account of an evolving situation, allocate reasoning effort before relevant opportunities expire, and distinguish an authorized action from a plausible but outdated suggestion. We propose Zoetrope, a model-agnostic architecture for continuous multimodal perception, asynchronous reasoning, and bounded intervention. Its starting configuration samples every other frame of a video stream. Rather than equating this sampling frequency with the frequency or latency of complete reasoning, Zoetrope separates observation ingestion, temporal state maintenance, reasoning admission, and action execution. A versioned evidence store connects claims to timestamped observations; a deadline-aware scheduler allocates deeper inference; and an independent execution gate revalidates permissions and action-critical evidence before an intervention. The design supports both responsive questions and standing requests that require proactive notice or action, while perception continues during response generation. We formalize the distinction between throughput and freshness, specify bounded-memory and overload behavior, and develop a causal evaluation protocol that measures deadline-conditioned correctness, stale-state errors, interruption burden, and resource use. The central hypothesis is that explicit evidence validity and selective reasoning improve useful real-time performance over isolated frame analysis and asynchronous systems without freshness checks. This manuscript presents an architecture, analytical constraints, and an experimental plan; it reports no implementation measurements or benchmark results.

title: BUXORO HUDUDI O'ZBEK SHEVALARI VARIANTLARINI AVTOMATIK ANIQLASH USULLARI
abstract: Annotatsiya: Ushbu tezisda Buxoro hududi o‘zbek shevalarining fonetik, leksik va morfologik xususiyatlarini kompyuter lingvistikasi usullari yordamida avtomatik aniqlash va tasniflash masalalari yoritilgan. Shuningdek, shevalarga xos til birliklarini aniqlash, ularni standart o‘zbek tili birliklaridan farqlash hamda avtomatik tasniflash imkoniyatlari tahlil qilinadi. Buxoro shevalarining o‘ziga xos xususiyatlarini raqamli ma’lumotlar asosida qayta ishlash va lingvistik modellar yordamida tasniflash usullari ko‘rib chiqiladi. Olingan natijalar o‘zbek shevalarini kompyuter yordamida tadqiq etish, elektron lingvistik resurslar yaratish va shevalarning raqamli korpusini shakllantirish uchun muhim ahamiyat kasb etadi. Kalit so’zlar: kompyuter lingvistikasi, NLP, buxoro shevasi, dialektalogiya, avtomatik aniqlash, korpus lingvistikasi. Аннотация: В данной тезисной работе рассматриваются вопросы автоматического выявления и классификации фонетических, лексических и морфологических особенностей узбекских говоров Бухарского региона с использованием методов компьютерной лингвистики. Также анализируются возможности выявления языковых единиц, характерных для диалектов, их разграничения от единиц стандартного узбекского языка и автоматической классификации. Abstract: This thesis examines the automatic identification and classification of the phonetic, lexical, and morphological features of Uzbek dialects in the Bukhara region using computational linguistics methods. It also analyzes the possibilities of identifying dialect-specific linguistic units, distinguishing them from standard Uzbek language units, and classifying them automatically. The study considers methods for processing the distinctive features of Bukhara dialects based on digital data and classifying them using linguistic models. The results obtained are of significant importance for computer-assisted research on Uzbek dialects, the development of electronic linguistic resources, and the compilation of a digital corpus of Uzbek dialects. title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF TRADITIONAL ENDOSCOPY AND AI BASED SYSTEMS
abstract: Reliable gastric ulcer detection depends on both systematic endoscopic inspection and the quality of the recorded images. Motion blur, specular reflections, bubbles and mucosal debris can obscure lesion margins and compromise automated analysis. This paper compares conventional endoscopic evaluation with artificial intelligence assisted image interpretation through a focused literature based analysis and a proposed evaluation framework. It examines artifact mechanisms, preprocessing options, model selection and clinical oversight. The central conclusion is that automated detection should be coupled with image quality assessment and transparent reporting. Enhancement cannot recover tissue information that was never captured, and performance on selected clean images cannot establish clinical reliability. A patient separated evaluation, artifact stratification and external validation are therefore necessary before claims of diagnostic superiority can be made. No new clinical experiment or validated accuracy estimate is reported in this paper.

title: Building Customer Trust Through Responsible AI
abstract: Artificial intelligence now sits at the heart of digital marketing. Firms rely on it for everything from personalized product recommendations and automated customer conversations to predictive analytics, dynamic pricing, and real-time campaign adjustments. Yet these same capabilities carry real risks. Data is collected in ways customers may not expect. Algorithms can reflect hidden biases. Automated messages can veer into manipulation. And when customers sense any of this, trust is the first thing to go .Drawing on Trust Theory, Privacy Calculus Theory, Stakeholder Theory, Signaling Theory, and the Resource-Based View, the chapter sets out a framework that connects responsible AI practices to customer trust, marketing outcomes, and financial outcomes. The core argument is simple but important: responsible AI is not mainly a technical or compliance matter. It is a cross-functional marketing and financial capability that allows firms to build lasting customer relationships in markets where data is everywhere and trust is harder to earn than ever.

title: Feature-token clinical transformer for 24-h landmark mortality risk stratification in critically ill patients with heart failure: development and multicenter external validation
abstract: Background The first 24 h after ICU admission in critically ill patients with heart failure yield heterogeneous EHR evidence across vital signs, laboratory tests, treatments, organ support, and nurse-charted monitoring. Conventional scores and flat-vector ML models may not preserve individual variable identity or context. Methods We developed FTCT, encoding each predictor recorded during the first 24 h after ICU admission as a clinically tagged token (value, missingness, identity, group). MIMIC-IV (2008–2019) served for development, validation, and internal testing; eICU-CRD (2014–2015) served for external validation. Included were adults with heart failure, a complete 24-h ICU observation window, and known discharge status. The endpoint was in-hospital all-cause death. Results MIMIC-IV included 11,156 stays and 1,484 deaths, partitioned into training ( n = 7,809), validation ( n = 1,673), and internal test ( n = 1,674) sets. eICU-CRD included 9,837 stays and 1,319 deaths. FTCT achieved an AUROC of 0.849 (95% CI, 0.835–0.863) internally and 0.804 (0.788–0.820) externally. Patient-paired AUROC differences vs. XGBoost were 0.027 (0.011–0.043) internally and 0.032 (0.014–0.050) externally. A matched FT-Transformer-style baseline achieved an external AUROC of 0.781 (0.760–0.801). In eICU-CRD, FTCT achieved an AUPRC of 0.296 (0.278–0.314), Brier score of 0.091 (0.085–0.097), and expected calibration error of 0.036 (0.030–0.042). In a post hoc cohort-specific descriptive operating analysis targeting approximately 85% specificity, external sensitivity was 0.662 (0.636–0.687), positive predictive value 0.406 (0.385–0.427), negative predictive value 0.942 (0.937–0.947), and F1 score 0.503. Removing feature-token encoding produced the largest ablation loss in external AUROC (−0.031). Conclusions FTCT combines established feature-token Transformer modeling with clinical-group embeddings, explicit missingness representation, and group-aware pooling for 24-h landmark mortality risk stratification from structured EHR data recorded during the first 24 h after ICU admission. Its external validation and ablation results support prospective investigation, but do not yet demonstrate clinical utility, workflow integration, admission-time applicability, or autonomous use.

title: "LoRa RFFI Cross-Domain Dataset for Secure Device Authentication"
abstract: "This dataset contains raw Software Defined Radio baseband recordings and their processed spectrogram tensor counterparts for benchmarking Radio-Frequency Fingerprinting Identification (RFFI) models that perform physical-layer device authentication. Cross-domain fingerprint generalization and open-set rogue hardware rejection capacities are the main directions of research under consideration.The environment-pooled method is used for training the deep learning models in order to achieve invariance to the measurement conditions. The baseband recordings are not partitioned according to the measurement environment during training. Instead, the data was pooled from four distinct physical domains during the first step of model training. As a result, the deep learning models are forced to learn how to cancel out the characteristics of the communication channel and focus on the unique hardware distortions present in every transmitter.The dataset is further split into a three-stage pipeline for research purposes. The continuous baseband recordings, spectrogram tensors that have been regularized to standard computer vision sizes, and packets with regularized Zero-Forcing channel equalization can all be used as inputs. The latter, which is the training pool, contains hardware fingerprints with carrier frequency offset, phase noise, IQ imbalance software-induced distortions to generalize over transceivers. The open-set authentication is enabled by hold-out fingerprints of the authorized node and attack vectors in an entirely separate physical transceiver."

title: Experimental Data for Implementation-Aware Real-Time Benchmark of Incremental PI and Mamdani Fuzzy Logic Speed Control for a Brushed DC Motor
abstract: This dataset contains the experimental data supporting the manuscript entitled Implementation-Aware Real-Time Benchmark of Incremental PI and Mamdani Fuzzy Logic Speed Control for a Brushed DC Motor. The experiments compare an incremental proportional–integral controller and a fixed-rule Mamdani Type-1 fuzzy logic controller implemented on the same Texas Instruments TMS320F2812 DSP platform. Both controllers were evaluated using identical encoder feedback, QEP-based speed estimation, a 1 ms sampling period, PWM actuation, voltage-command limitation, supply conditions, measured channels, and KPI-extraction procedures. The dataset covers nominally no-load step-response experiments at reference speeds of 955 rpm and 6685 rpm. The recorded quantities include reference speed, measured motor speed, voltage-equivalent command monitor, and armature current. The associated performance indicators include 10–90% rise time, percentage overshoot, ±1% settling time, transient peak armature current, and steady-state armature current. The files are organized by controller and operating point. A README file describes the file structure, variable names, units, controller parameters, and the procedure used to reproduce the reported performance indicators and figures.

title: Accurate gap control of 3D-integrated superconducting quantum circuits using asymmetric indium architecture and multi-angle flip-chip bonding
abstract: Flip-chip 3D integration is a key enabling technology for overcoming the routing and layout constraints of planar superconducting quantum processors, but it requires accurate and uniform control of the inter-chip spacing while preserving qubit coherence. In conventional processes, thick indium bumps are deposited symmetrically on both chips, while dedicated spacers are introduced to limit the residual tilt. Here, we present a flip-chip bonding process based on an asymmetric indium architecture, combining $20\,μ\mathrm{m}$ thick indium bumps on the control chip with $200\,\mathrm{nm}$ thin indium pads on the qubit chip. Using electrical and microwave measurements, we demonstrate low resistance and low loss indium interconnects, and show that transmon qubits integrated with this process reach relaxation and coherence times of $T_1=(159\pm14)\,μ\mathrm{s}$ and $T_{\mathrm{2,echo}}=(294\pm42)\,μ\mathrm{s}$, respectively, comparable to planar devices. Combined with a multi angle compression procedure that suppresses systematic tilt, this approach reduces the average post bonding tilt to $(20\pm12)\,μ\mathrm{rad}$. These results establish an asymmetric indium architecture combined with multi angle compression as a robust, coherence preserving route toward 3D integrated superconducting quantum processors.

title: CoViG: Coarsened Vision GNN for Image Classification
abstract: Although Graph Neural Networks are widely used in various domains, they remained mostly unexplored in computer vision. Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers were leading the field, until the quite recent introduction of Vision Graphs (ViG) that treat images as a set of nodes and apply graph convolution on their k-NN graphs. ViGs show impressive accuracy on image classification but their computational cost remains relatively high. Inspired by optimization methods for GNNs, we present CoViG, a novel approach combining graph coarsening and ViGs. Our method introduces an additional MinCUT pooling step within the Grapher component of intermediate ViG blocks. By simplifying the intermediate graphs and thus decreasing the number of nodes of specific blocks, our approach considerably reduces the computational cost of ViG during inference. We evaluated our approach on ImageNet with several ViG architectures, and we obtained accuracies equivalent to the original ViG models with only about 51\% of FLOPs.

title: Evidence Field for Histopathology: Cross-Centre Evaluation and Replayable Spatial Decisions
abstract: Histopathology classifiers must transfer across acquisition sites while exposing evidence that can be checked independently. Evidence Field couples learned image measurements and spatial classification with a native covering-program record. We evaluate this architecture on all 455,954 released CAMELYON17-WILDS patches, using patient-separated source partitions and two held-out hospital centres. Eighteen from-scratch fits compare four Evidence Field objectives with residual convolutional and compact vision-transformer classifiers. Checkpoints, temperatures and review thresholds are selected using source validation. The source-selected paired-cross-entropy ensemble achieves areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.9356 and 0.9453, with accuracies of 84.46% and 86.77% at the two held-out centres. Corresponding convolutional values are 0.7352 and 0.7656, and transformer values are 0.8502 and 0.7924. Evidence Field has 10,550 trainable parameters per member and additionally returns selected covers, signed region and interaction terms, contextual dependencies and independently reconstructible predictions. Patient-cluster intervals, calibration, source-fixed review policies and recorded training resources characterize the results. A 340-image, three-member audit reconstructs probability mixtures and 6,120 class programs under three rigid views. The evaluation supports cross-centre discrimination and reproducible computation for these implemented models; unequal family tuning, previously examined public targets and limited patient groups constrain broader interpretation.

title: The Co-Evolution of Quantum Physics and Finance
abstract: Quantum physics and finance are often connected through mathematical analogy or promises of computational acceleration. This article develops an alternative account of asymmetric co-evolution. A selective conceptual synthesis distinguishes shared mathematical ancestry, explicit transfer, and reciprocal innovation across uncertainty, valuation, measurement, computation, and monetary security. Quantum theory supplies representational and computational possibilities; financial problems impose constraints that can redirect quantum information research. Documented feedback is strongest in algorithm design and cryptographic tasks. This article proposes testable research directions concerning investor judgment, financial validation, decision-relevant computational advantage, market adoption, and quantum money. Progress requires reciprocal discipline: quantum methods must satisfy financial restrictions, while finance must incorporate the physical and computational conditions governing information.

title: The Dark Side of Generative AI in Marketing: AI-Generated False and Misleading Advertising and Its Consumer Consequences
abstract: Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming advertising by enabling marketers to create persuasive text, images, and other promotional content rapidly and at lower cost. At the same time, the ability of generative systems to produce highly realistic content creates concerns about deception, misinformation, transparency, and the credibility of consumer-facing information. The present study examines the consumer consequences of AI-generated false and misleading advertising, with particular emphasis on hallucinated product claims. The study focuses on whether AI-generated hallucinated product claims influence perceived deception, AI skepticism, and perceived information reliability, and whether these consumer responses subsequently shape purchase intention. Drawing on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, the study conceptualizes hallucinated product claims as the stimulus, the three consumer evaluations as the organism, and purchase intention as the response. A quantitative, cross-sectional, deductive research design was adopted. Data were collected from 320 business-school students and faculty members through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale, and the model was assessed using SmartPLS. The reported measurement results show Cronbach's alpha values above 0.70, composite reliability above the stated threshold, and average variance extracted above 0.50 for all constructs, indicating acceptable reliability and convergent validity. The reported discriminant-validity matrix also supports construct distinctiveness. The structural model reports a VIF range of 1.47-2.24 and an R² of 0.421 for purchase intention. Four of the six hypotheses are supported. AI-generated hallucinated product claims significantly increase perceived deception and significantly reduce perceived information reliability. Perceived deception significantly reduces purchase intention, while perceived information reliability significantly increases purchase intention. The paths from hallucinated product claims to AI skepticism and from AI skepticism to purchase intention are not statistically significant. The findings indicate that message-level judgments of deception and information reliability are more consequential for purchase intention in the reported model than generalized skepticism toward AI. evidence.title: The Dark Side of Generative AI in Marketing: AI-Generated False and Misleading Advertising and Its Consumer Consequences
evidence.abstract: Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming advertising by enabling marketers to create persuasive text, images, and other promotional content rapidly and at lower cost. At the same time, the ability of generative systems to produce highly realistic content creates concerns about deception, misinformation, transparency, and the credibility of consumer-facing information. The present study examines the consumer consequences of AI-generated false and misleading advertising, with particular emphasis on hallucinated product claims. The study focuses on whether AI-generated hallucinated product claims influence perceived deception, AI skepticism, and perceived information reliability, and whether these consumer responses subsequently shape purchase intention. Drawing on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, the study conceptualizes hallucinated product claims as the stimulus, the three consumer evaluations as the organism, and purchase intention as the response. A quantitative, cross-sectional, deductive research design was adopted. Data were collected from 320 business-school students and faculty members through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale, and the model was assessed using SmartPLS. The reported measurement results show Cronbach's alpha values above 0.70, composite reliability above the stated threshold, and average variance extracted above 0.50 for all constructs, indicating acceptable reliability and convergent validity. The reported discriminant-validity matrix also supports construct distinctiveness. The structural model reports a VIF range of 1.47-2.24 and an R² of 0.421 for purchase intention. Four of the six hypotheses are supported. AI-generated hallucinated product claims significantly increase perceived deception and significantly reduce perceived information reliability. Perceived deception significantly reduces purchase intention, while perceived information reliability significantly increases purchase intention. The paths from hallucinated product claims to AI skepticism and from AI skepticism to purchase intention are not statistically significant. The findings indicate that message-level judgments of deception and information reliability are more consequential for purchase intention in the reported model than generalized skepticism toward AI. The study extends the S-O-R perspective to the dark side of GenAI in advertising and highlights the importance of factual verification, transparency, human oversight, disclosure, and consumer AI literacy. title: Propuestas novedosas para incrementar y depurar el repertorio dramático de Luis Vélez de Guevara
abstract: El repertorio dramático de Luis Vélez de Guevara nos ha llegado casi en su totalidad tras las correspondientes adaptaciones escénicas e impresas y sin control de la transmisión por parte del poeta. A través de métodos estilométricos ofrecemos propuestas de inclusión y exclusión de obras teatrales al corpus velecista. Se ofrece información sobre 58 piezas que nos han llegado con atribuciones a distintos autores, entre los que figura Luis Vélez, y en las que la estilometría ha detectado su huella, o su ausencia, cuando las fuentes primarias no generaban dudas. Lo más interesante son las 15 atribuciones, muy seguras desde la estilometría, que se relacionan con el dramaturgo, algunas ya señaladas con anterioridad por otros métodos y pistas, lo cual da mucha solidez a lo que aquí se propone. También son relevantes las 29 obras que son rechazadas por esta técnica. Con estas sumas y restas finales, Luis Vélez sigue siendo uno de los dramaturgos con mayor número de obras dramáticas conservadas, en torno al centenar, solo superado por Lope y Calderón.

title: Radial–Angular Feature Shaping with an eXtra-Node and Prototype-Based Cosine Similarity Under Adversarial Perturbations
abstract: Adversarial perturbations can alter neural-network predictions, motivating closer analysis of the geometry of learned feature representations. For a given local displacement in feature space, small-norm feature vectors can undergo larger first-order directional changes than larger-norm vectors. This study examines this geometric effect in a two-dimensional (2D) bottleneck and proposes a composite objective that regulates feature radius and class-aligned direction. A norm-dependent auxiliary eXtra-node contributes a direct outward feature-gradient component for nonzero features near the origin, whereas a prototype-based cosine similarity (PCS) term aligns features with normalized classifier-weight directions. An exact comparison with semantic cross-entropy further shows that auxiliary softmax normalization introduces an additional semantic-normalization coupling term with generally mixed radial and tangential components. Experiments on a 10-class subset of ImageNet with six matched CNN and Transformer backbones show that the proposed objective increases both the mean feature radius and the mean similarity to the ground-truth class prototype. Under the FGSM, PGD, FDA, UAP, and DeepFool settings used in the experiments, post-attack accuracy is higher in 26 of 30 backbone–procedure comparisons, while mean clean accuracy changes from 98.69% to 98.15%. These results show that the eXtra-node–PCS objective reshapes the 2D representation in the intended radial and angular directions and support further investigation in standard high-dimensional feature spaces and under adaptive attack evaluation.

title: LWE-Based Threshold Key Management with Dynamic Enrollment and Share Refresh
abstract: We present a trusted-dealer Learning with Errors (LWE)-based threshold key-management framework that separates the public-key layer from threshold-share maintenance. The coordinator generates one LWE public key PK=(A,b),b=As+e(modq) and distributes the same secret vector through coordinate-wise Shamir (t,n) sharing. Dynamic membership is restricted to enrollment: a new participant obtains an evaluation of the existing sharing polynomial, so enrollment does not rotate the secret or change the LWE key pair. Share refresh uses participant-generated degree-(t−1) vector polynomials with zero constant term. Their evaluations are exchanged over authenticated private channels and added locally, preserving the same secret without interpolation or accumulation of LWE error. This paper formalizes exact threshold recovery, single-epoch share privacy, and cross-epoch share-snapshot privacy under a restricted post-refresh observation model with hidden refresh state and effective erasure. It also introduces an explicit epoch-consistency rule so that recovery never mixes shares from different refresh epochs and derives communication and computation costs separately for setup, enrollment, refresh, and recovery. Hash-based commitments and authenticated private channels are treated as integrity and delivery mechanisms rather than as substitutes for maliciously secure verifiable secret sharing (VSS). The post-quantum claim is conditional on concrete validation of the selected LWE parameter tuple. Dealerless distributed key generation (DKG), coordinator-compromise proactive security, participant departure, threshold changes, and a complete quantum random oracle model (QROM) reduction remain outside the present security claims.

title: Motion- and Gravity-Aware Feedforward 3D Reconstruction
abstract: Feed-forward transformer models have recently achieved strong performance in multi-view 3D reconstruction, but they still rely primarily on appearance-based attention and often struggle in dynamic scenes with weak geometric cues. In this work, we introduce a motion- and gravity-aware framework under the Learning Using Privileged Information (LUPI) paradigm. During training, residual optical flow and gravity direction are provided as privileged signals to guide geometric representation learning; during inference, the model uses standard visual inputs only. We integrate these priors into transformer backbones with lightweight architectural changes, preserving feed-forward efficiency. Experiments on standard benchmarks show consistent gains in reconstruction accuracy and robustness, especially in scenes with dynamic objects, ambiguous structure, and challenging camera motion. Our analysis further shows that the optimal injection stage is backbone-dependent: middle-layer integration is generally preferable for VGGT, while late-stage integration is more effective for π3. These results suggest that LUPI offers a practical way to inject motion and physical priors into feed-forward 3D reconstruction without increasing test-time complexity.

title: Quantum control of solid state qubits via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The use of reinforcement learning (RL) in the design of quantum control strategies for pulse level control of NISQ era quantum devices is attracting growing interest. Model-free RL, not requiring preexisting knowledge of the physical system, acts as a black-box optimization tool well suited for noisy devices. In this work, we provide a simulation-based analysis of the performance of model-free RL for state preparation and qubit gate design in a challenging setup: indirect control of NV nuclear spins in a spin-bath. In particular, the spin-bath is modeled via the generalized cluster correlation expansion accounting for magnetic impurities and intra-bath interactions. We analyze the performance of the RL agents by performing simulations with minimally observable environments and noisy, sparse rewards as introduced in (Phys. Rev. X 12, 011059), and compare them to other state-of-the-art black-box optimization tools.

title: Seeing Both the Forest and the Trees: Reusing Holistic 3D Priors for Part-Decomposed Generation
abstract: Generating 3D assets with explicit parts requires two properties at once: geometric detail inside each part and structural coherence across the whole object. Recent image-conditioned 3D generation models adopt a structured 3D representation that anchors tokens to explicit spatial positions, capturing both properties, but their output remains a single fused mesh. We ask how a part-decomposed generation model can inherit both properties of these holistic priors, and answer with STRUCTPARTS, a framework whose core technical contribution is a dual-frame coordinate interleaving mechanism: each shape latent is interpreted under both a part-local and an object-global reference frame, and processed through a global-local inter-leaved transformer that simultaneously reuses the prior's geometric detail at the part scale and its structural coherence at the whole-object scale. As its structural input, STRUCTPARTS uses a segmented mesh scaffold, a coarse mesh paired with a face-level segmentation mask kept entirely within the prior's native 3D representation. With only lightweight finetuning, both intra-part detail and inter-part coherence emerge from the same pretrained weights. On PartObjaverse-Tiny, STRUCTPARTS matches or surpasses prior part-decomposed models at a fraction of their training cost, while naturally supporting part-mesh refinement and part-level editing.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in Pairwise Difference Learning for Classification
abstract: Instead of learning a mapping from instances to outcomes in the standard way, the key idea of pairwise difference learning (PDL) is to learn a function that takes two instances as input and predicts the difference between the respective outcomes. Given a function of this kind, predictions for a query instance are derived from every training example and then averaged. We propose a version of PDL for the task of classification and propose a suitable meta-learning technique for this purpose. Moreover, we address the problem of uncertainty quantification, i.e., of representing and quantifying the uncertainty of a PDL classifier's predictions in a faithful manner. Building on recent work on the decomposition of total uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components, we propose different ways of extending corresponding measures to the setting of PDL, depending on how and to what extent uncertainty is represented by the underlying base learner. In large-scale empirical studies, we analyze both the predictive accuracy and the uncertainty awareness of our PDL classifier.

title: SIEVE: Overcoming Topological Obstruction in Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: We identify a theoretical incompatibility between 3D point cloud masked autoencoding and SE(3)-equivariant networks. We prove that standard masking triggers a topological collapse, effectively forcing the model to hallucinate orientation without a reference frame. To resolve this, we introduce SIEVE (Scalar Invariant Extraction Via Equivariance), an SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised framework that compresses point cloud geometry into invariant scalar embeddings. At its core is the spherical projection mask, which preserves global pose while obfuscating local semantics, sidestepping the obstruction by construction. Experiments confirm that SIEVE circumvents the predicted collapse where constant and noise masks fail. On downstream point cloud tasks, the resulting embeddings improve over coordinate-based baselines and hand-crafted geometric descriptors, with the largest gains on generalization to unseen shape categories.

title: Solving the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem Using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm: A Benchmark Against Classical Guided Local Search
abstract: The Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) is a combinatorial optimization problem that can be formulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem, making it a potential application for near-term quantum optimization. This paper benchmarks the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA, p = 2) against Google OR-Tools Guided Local Search on a seeded instance with three customers and two vehicles. The study examines the QUBO formulation, energy spectrum, optimization behavior, penalty weights, Hamiltonian scaling, and circuit depths. The experiments show that the tested QAOA configurations do not reliably concentrate probability on optimal solutions. The classical solver identifies the optimal solution for the selected instance. The study provides a reproducible baseline and discusses limitations and future research directions. The findings are limited to the tested instance, formulation, and optimization configurations.

title: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): An Adaptive Framework for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering
abstract: This paper presents a proposed Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for adaptive, evidence-grounded question answering using large language models (LLMs). Unlike conventional single-pass RAG systems, the proposed framework incorporates query planning, retrieval, tool selection, evidence evaluation, answer generation, and self-reflection. The framework uses a bounded feedback loop to improve evidence retrieval when the initial results are insufficient or conflicting. It aims to produce answers supported by relevant source citations while communicating uncertainty when reliable evidence is unavailable. The paper discusses the system architecture, workflow, algorithmic control logic, evaluation methodology, security, privacy, and governance considerations. It also proposes evaluation metrics for answer quality, retrieval effectiveness, factual grounding, latency, computational cost, and component-level ablation studies. Potential applications include research assistance, document question answering, enterprise knowledge management, customer support, and data analysis. This work presents a conceptual framework and proposed evaluation plan. Implementation, benchmark experiments, and measured performance improvements are not reported. Keywords: Agentic RAG, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Large Language Models, AI Agents, Evidence-Grounded Question Answering, Adaptive Retrieval, Self-Reflection.

title: Adaptive Learning and Collaborative Adaptive Learning Between World Self-Models and World Mutual-Models: A Dynamic Switching Framework
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental dynamics that support prediction, simulation, planning, and decision-making. However, learning within a world model and learning through interactions among multiple world models are often treated as separate design choices. Independent adaptation can preserve model-specific knowledge and reduce communication overhead, whereas collaborative adaptation can facilitate knowledge transfer, error correction, and the identification of shared environmental regularities. Neither mode is universally optimal across all tasks, environments, and stages of learning. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for adaptive learning and collaborative adaptive learning between World Self-Models and World Mutual-Models. The framework distinguishes autonomous model adaptation from inter-model collaborative adaptation and introduces a dynamic switching mechanism that selects between these modes according to predictive uncertainty, model disagreement, learning progress, environmental change, expected collaboration benefit, and coordination cost. Rather than requiring continuous collaboration or permanent isolation, the framework treats learning mode selection as a sequential decision problem. A world model can independently update its internal dynamics, selectively request information from other world models, incorporate externally obtained evidence, or return to autonomous learning when collaboration is unnecessary or counterproductive. The proposed architecture includes model-specific state representations, predictive dynamics, uncertainty estimation, collaborative information exchange, adaptive mode selection, and feedback-based evaluation. A formal objective is developed to balance predictive performance, adaptation speed, robustness, knowledge diversity, and computational efficiency. The paper also proposes implementation procedures, research hypotheses, comparative baselines, evaluation metrics, and ablation studies. The framework is intended for model-based reinforcement learning, embodied agents, robotic systems, and other environments in which multiple predictive world models learn related or interacting dynamics. It does not require large language models as its fundamental computational substrate. The proposed framework is a research design rather than an empirically validated algorithm; its effectiveness and novelty relative to existing adaptive multi-agent world-model methods require systematic experimental investigation.

title: ЦИФРОВОЙ ТЕКСТ-АНАЛИЗ ЭЛЕКТРОННЫХ АМБУЛАТОРНЫХ ЗАПИСЕЙ В КЛИНИКО-ЭПИДЕМИОЛОГИЧЕСКОЙ ХАРАКТЕРИСТИКЕ СИНДРОМА КОНСКОГО ХВОСТА: ВОЗМОЖНОСТИ И ОГРАНИЧЕНИЯ ЦИФРОВОЙ МЕДИЦИНЫ
abstract: В работе на примере ретроспективного анализа синдрома конского хвоста (СКХ) продемонстрирован потенциал цифровых методов текст-майнинга неструктурированных электронных амбулаторных записей для быстрой клинико-эпидемиологической характеристики редкой неврологической патологии. Из массива 3054 визитов неврологической клиники методом ключевого поиска и дедупликации сформирована когорта из 323 уникальных пациентов с диагнозом «синдром конского хвоста» (10,6% от всех визитов). Обоснована перспективность интеграции правило-ориентированного и ИИ/NLP-ассистированного анализа медицинских записей, телемедицинского мониторинга тазовых функций и биомаркер-ориентированной индивидуализированной диагностики в рамках концепции цифровой медицины.

title: Optimizing the Privacy Accuracy Trade-off in Data Stream Mining Using Random Cycle Cumulative Noise Addition
abstract: Data stream mining has become increasingly important as a result of the continuous generation of data in real world applications including healthcare monitoring, sensor networks, transportation systems and online services. While stream classification techniques provide strong predictive performance, publishing or processing such streams raises serious privacy concerns. Perturbation based privacy preserving data stream mining (PPDSM) methods address this issue by adding noise to the data before it is analyzed. Cumulative noise addition accumulates noise across a fixed-size cycle of records give a favourable privacy–accuracy trade-off compared with independent noise addition. However, a fixed cycle size introduces a predictable and periodic structure in the perturbation process. This paper proposes Random-Cycle Cumulative Noise Addition (RC-CNA), a perturbation mechanism that adds noise to random cycle sizes instead of fix-cycle size. RC-CNA is evaluated against the fixedcycle model. The proposed method raises classification accuracy, lowers privacy breach probability, and achieves the overall Privacy–Accuracy trade-off. Proposed method indicates that randomizing the cycle size, combined with the modulation, is a practical improvement that simultaneously strengthens privacy protection and improves classification utility.

title: Context-Aware Cooperative Gating for Knowledge-Controlled Value Factorization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under partial observability requires decentralized agents to act from incomplete local information. Value-decomposition methods such as VDN and QMIX do not control when teammate-related knowledge may influence an agent’s local utility, and an uncontrolled teammate-conditioned term can distort decisions at timesteps where no ally is observable. We propose CA-QMIX, a context-aware value factorization method that uses ally visibility as a knowledge signal for decentralized agent control. Each agent combines an individual decision branch with an attention-based cooperative knowledge branch through a visibility-conditioned gate that scales the cooperative contribution and is hard-masked to zero when no ally is observable. The gated utilities are combined by a QMIX-style monotonic mixer, which we prove preserves Individual-Global-Max consistency, and a mixer-level Δ-Q regularizer discourages cooperative corrections that lower the greedy value of the base branch. Experiments on seven SMAC v1 and SMAC v2 scenarios against six value-decomposition baselines show that CA-QMIX attains the highest mean final win rate and the best mean rank over the seven scenarios and improves on QMIX in all three randomized SMAC v2 scenarios. Ablations show that most of the gain comes from the cooperative branch, that its visibility conditioning helps when correctly aligned (misaligned visibility degrades performance under randomized placement), and that the form of the gate is not critical: a binary gate suffices and the hard no-ally mask has no measurable cost.

title: Temporal Periodic Image Registration with Implicit Neural Representations
abstract: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) have recently gained popularity for their ability to model functions using simple and lightweight networks. These methods have also proven effective in deformable image registration. In this work, we extend INRs for deformable image registration to the domain of temporal image registration, focusing on periodic temporal image sequences. Our approach, Temporal-IDIR, optimizes a single INR to model deformations across all frames in a temporal image sequence simultaneously, allowing for self-regularization through its own deformation predictions. To achieve this, we introduce a temporal consistency loss that penalizes discrepancies between direct source-to-target transformations and those traversing intermediate frames. We evaluate our framework on the DIR-LAB dataset, using the target registration error (TRE) between annotated and moved landmarks as the metric. Here, we achieve a TRE of 1.03 mm, outperforming other INR-based registration methods. Additionally, our framework supports smooth interpolation between time frames by estimating deformations between the given input frames. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/MMLowes/Temporal_INR.

title: RoPE-Flow: Monocular Vision-based Robot Pose Estimation via 2D Graph-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. However, recovering 3D structural features from 2D observations remains a challenging task. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering or involve sophisticated 2D-3D registration which suffers from projection ambiguity, accumulated errors for distal joints and imbalanced learning for different joints. In this work, we propose RoPE-Flow, an end-to-end flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator, which embeds a learnable adjacency map to generate condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-Depth Loss for topological consistency and scale stability, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with mutiple cameras. Besides, we establish a novel cross-scene benchmark to demonstrate the outstanding performance of RoPE-Flow on zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Meanwhile, animated visualizations are shown on the website: ropeflow.netlify.app

title: Leveraging Large Language Model Token Probabilities for Literature Review Abstract Filtering
abstract: Grasping the latest knowledge in any field has become increasingly challenging given the rapid pace of modern publishing. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly embedding models and large language models (LLMs), provide promising tools to aid researchers in the filtration and identification of the most relevant literature. However, there is little practical guidance on how to incorporate LLMs into literature reviews, and there are not yet direct comparisons of embedding models versus generative approaches. In this work, we compare these methods using small local LLMs for literature screening on both a simple dataset containing distinct categories and a more complex example with abstracts obtained from the Web of Science. We find that embedding models perform strongly for simple, well-separated queries due to their robustness and computational efficiency. For more complex filtering tasks, generative approaches based on token probabilities can achieve competitive or superior performance, but only when properly calibrated and when token-level outputs are interpreted as continuous scores rather than binary decisions. However, we show these methods are highly sensitive to prompt formulation, token conventions, and threshold selection.

title: Does Grounding Argument Strengths in Evidence Text Help Claim Verification? A Study of Token-Anchored Arguments vs. ArgRAG
abstract: This paper investigates whether grounding argument strengths in evidence text improves automated claim verification. Building on ArgRAG, the study introduces the Token Argument Model (TAM), which represents retrieved evidence as shorter arguments anchored to verbatim text and estimates argument strength using a Natural Language Inference (NLI) model. TAM is evaluated across four experimental settings using PubHealth and SciFact. Results show that grounding argument strengths does not consistently improve claim-verification accuracy over uniform argument strengths, and randomly shuffled strength scores achieve comparable results. However, representing evidence as shorter, quote-anchored arguments improves accuracy by 6.0 percentage points on PubHealth in the top-5 retrieval setting. The findings suggest that improving argument representation can be more beneficial than assigning model-derived strength scores. Reproducibility note: The reproduced ArgRAG baseline does not match the accuracy reported in the original paper. Results should therefore be interpreted as relative comparisons within this experimental setup, not as direct comparisons with the original benchmark performance.

title: A Hybrid RAG-Based Framework for Improved Information Retrieval from Long Documents via Summarization and Question Answering
abstract: We present an integrated system, which is a mix of summarization as well as Question Answering (QA) to boost the performance regarding information retrieval (IR) for long and domain-intensive documents. This work creates a synergistic relationship between both tasks to enhance retrieval efficiency and quality of answers, unlike previous studies focusing separately on either summarization or QA. The framework proposed is comprised of three stages. First, it involves summarization that is used for condensing documents, maintaining their key semantic content. Second, it employs a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture, where the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model is used for the retrieval stage, while T5 and BART-Large-CNN models are utilized for the generation stage. Lastly, answers generated are put into comparison with a baseline system which works with complete document processing without summarization. Results at the NIPS dataset reveal that integrating summarization with QA significantly improves each summary informativeness and answer accuracy. To investigate the impact of summarization inside the retrieval pipeline, two complementary eventualities are explored. First, Proactive Summarization as an Indexing Tool (Summarization-First) plays summarization earlier than the indexing and retrieval stages to reduce record size and improve retrieval performance while keeping semantic relevance. Second, Query-Guided Contextual Summarization (Retrieval-First Summarization) applies summarization after the retrieval level, wherein only the retrieved relevant passages are summarized in step with consumer question for generating more targeted and context-conscious solutions. These two scenarios enable a comparative analysis of the way the position of summarization within RAG pipeline impacts retrieval efficiency as well as solution era quality. title: AEDS: Adaptive edge‐difference shaping for piecewise‐stationary sparse‐reward reinforcement learning
abstract: Abstract Sparse‐reward tasks with piecewise‐stationary topology shifts challenge reinforcement learning. Continuous spectral shaping biases agents toward geometric extrema and can delay adaptation when bottlenecks move. We propose adaptive edge‐difference shaping (AEDS), a spectral reward‐shaping method that focuses exploration on structural bottlenecks. AEDS triggers a direction‐agnostic intrinsic reward only when the agent crosses the sign‐flip boundary of the dynamically updated Fiedler vector. An episodic gating mechanism limits rewarded crossings and bounds the cumulative intrinsic return. Within each stationary phase, AEDS induces an augmented Markov decision process to which the standard tabular Q‐learning convergence theorem applies. We evaluate AEDS on grid environments with shifting bottlenecks and geometric traps. Across the evaluation, AEDS performs strongly in several bottleneck‐oriented settings, while count‐based exploration or well‐oriented dense spectral shaping can be preferable in other regimes. These results support a focused scope for AEDS in bottleneck‐oriented sparse‐reward grid tasks.

title: Oblivis: A Framework for Delegated and Efficient Oblivious Transfer
abstract: As database deployments shift toward cloud platforms and edge devices, thin clients need to securely retrieve sensitive records without leaking their query intent or metadata to the proxies that mediate access. Oblivious Transfer (OT) is a core tool for private retrieval, yet existing OTs assume direct client–database interaction and lack support for delegated querying or lightweight clients. We present Oblivis, a modular framework of new OT protocols that enable delegated, privacy-preserving query execution. Oblivis allows clients to retrieve database records without direct access, protects against leakage to both databases and proxies, and is designed with practical efficiency in mind. Its components include: (1) Delegated-Query OT, which permits secure outsourcing of query generation; (2) Multi-Receiver OT for merged, cloud-hosted databases; (3) a compiler producing constant-size responses suitable for thin clients; and (4) Supersonic OT, a proxy-based, information- theoretic, and highly efficient 1-out-of-2 OT. The protocols are formally defined and proven secure in the simulation-based paradigm, under non-colluding assumption. We implement and empirically evaluate Supersonic OT. It achieves at least a 92× speedup over a highly efficient 1-out-of-2 OT, and a 2.6×–106× speedup over a standard OT extension across 200–100,000 invocations. Our implementation further shows that Supersonic OT remains efficient even on constrained hardware, e.g., it completes an end-to-end transfer in 1.36 ms on a Raspberry Pi 4.

title: People and algorithms: Working with AI in marketing
abstract: Artificial Intelligence is no longer a distant technological trend in marketing. Used well, AI can boost marketing practice. Without an informed, critical approach to use, it can reproduce bias, generate misleading insights, weaken creativity, and create serious ethical, legal, and security risks. This handbook has been prepared to support your work with Artificial Intelligence in marketing in a thoughtful, creative, and responsible way. Its goal is not only to introduce AI tools and concepts, but also to help you develop the judgment required to use them effectively. The handbook is primarily addressed to marketing students at the master’s level. It has been devel­oped by marketing departments from European universities who are witnessing how AI the trans­formation of the profession and deciding how marketing education should respond to this change. The chapters are designed to connect conceptual understanding with practical application, helping students prepare for marketing roles in which AI will be part of everyday work. This handbook is the result of collaboration between academics from Poznań University of Econom­ics and Business (Poland, project leader) and Corvinus University of Budapest (Hungary), University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria, Stockholm School of Economics (Sweden), Complutense Universi­ty of Madrid (Spain), Polytechnic University of Marche, Ancona (Italy), University of Zagreb, Faculty of Economicsand Business (Croatia), and University of Perpignan (France). This handbook has been supported by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange under the NAWA Strategic Partnership program, project BNI/PST/2023/1/00082 DIGIT: People and algorithms in organisations.

This handbook has been prepared to support your work with Artificial Intelligence in marketing in a thoughtful, creative, and responsible way. Its goal is not only to introduce AI tools and concepts, but also to help you develop the judgment required to use them effectively. The handbook is primarily addressed to marketing students at the master’s level. It has been devel­oped by marketing departments from European universities who are witnessing how AI the trans­formation of the profession and deciding how marketing education should respond to this change. The chapters are designed to connect conceptual understanding with practical application, helping students prepare for marketing roles in which AI will be part of everyday work. This handbook is the result of collaboration between academics from Poznań University of Econom­ics and Business (Poland, project leader) and Corvinus University of Budapest (Hungary), University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria, Stockholm School of Economics (Sweden), Complutense Universi­ty of Madrid (Spain), Polytechnic University of Marche, Ancona (Italy), University of Zagreb, Faculty of Economicsand Business (Croatia), and University of Perpignan (France). This handbook has been supported by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange under the NAWA Strategic Partnership program, project BNI/PST/2023/1/00082 DIGIT: People and algorithms in organisations.

title: Physics-Aware Distillation of a Grid Foundation Model for Real-Time Edge Inference
abstract: Grid foundation models (GridFMs) are graph transformers pretrained on a masked power-flow objective, and evaluate power flow orders of magnitude faster than an iterative solver. Their size, however, targets data-centre inference, whereas low-inertia operation increasingly asks for inference at the edge, next to the measurement, at batch size one and within a single synchrophasor (PMU) reporting frame. We distil a 20.1M-parameter, 12-layer GridFM teacher into a 0.62M-parameter, 6-layer student, a $32.5\times$ parameter reduction at half the message-passing depth, using an objective that combines the masked power-flow loss with output, physics-residual, latent-state and attention transfer. The physics-residual term, which matches the teacher's power-residual profile, has not previously been applied to typed power-grid graphs. We evaluate on a renewable variant of the IEEE 118-bus benchmark grid in which 26 of the conventional (synchronous) generators are replaced by inverter-based renewables with battery flexibility and standardised reactive-power limits (IEEE 1547), giving $97\,529$ physically valid (AC-OPF-feasible) operating scenarios, and we ablate all eight combinations of the transfer terms, reporting accuracy against ground truth and fidelity to the teacher separately. Distillation lowers student error on all four predicted quantities, by up to $48\%$ on active-power dispatch, and every distilled student is more accurate than its teacher on reactive-power dispatch. The gain is largely carried by the output matching term. The physics-residual term, in the layer-aggregated form used here, is consistently harmful, which we attribute to the spatial averaging it applies to a bus-level residual field. The resulting student is $32.5\times$ smaller in parameter count and has half the message-passing depth, making it a candidate for subsequent edge-device benchmarking.

title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance for TI2I Flow Matching
abstract: We study Text-and-Image-to-Image (TI2I) flow matching methods for controllable image editing. In a broader generative modeling context, Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) is established as a key component responsible for high quality outputs. However, we argue that its role in TI2I modeling is poorly understood. Specifically, we make the surprising observation that the CFG mechanism is implicitly harmful for editing in the noisy phase of flow modeling, hindering instruction following and controllability. We propose a simple correction in the early flow steps, enabling a richer alignment-preservation tradeoff at no extra cost. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated on both pixel-space and latent TI2I flows.

title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation in S3-Compatible Object Storage under Client Concurrency
abstract: Data encrypted today with classical public-key algorithms could be decrypted once large quantum computers exist. Cloud object stores keep data for years, so the client-side encryption that protects it must move to post-quantum algorithms such as ML-KEM, which adds a key-encapsulation step and a larger ciphertext to every stored object. So far, the cost of ML-KEM has been measured for the algorithm on its own and for securing network connections, but not for encrypting each object in a storage system that serves many clients at once. It has therefore been unclear whether ML-KEM slows such a system, under which conditions, and why. We address this problem by measuring per-object ML-KEM against classical key exchange on an S3-compatible object store, with two client implementations, two processor types and up to 500 concurrent workers, using pre-registered experiments and statistical equivalence tests. ML-KEM reduced throughput only when the client's processor was at or near full load, with one unexplained exception, and then by 4.0 to 4.9% in our main client. Controlled experiments on one processor type traced most of that loss to the way the software library was called, and a second, native client showed that the size of the loss depends on the implementation. The lasting cost is storage: 1,056 more bytes per object than with classical key exchange. The results cover two clients, one single-node store and one cloud provider.

title: Loud and Clear: Making Visual Evidence Count in Multimodal Document RAG
abstract: Multimodal document retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has focused largely on retrieval, yet its answers depend on how well a vision-language model reads the retrieved pages. We find that evidence in retrieved pages remains underused even when the correct pages are retrieved. On SciEGQA oracle pages, five prior methods give the generator 0.7K to 2.7K visual tokens per query on average under a common image processor, yet raising the page-only budget from 1K to 32K improves accuracy by 15.22 points. At a fixed 16K budget, adding ground-truth crops improves accuracy by 3.75 points over page-only input. We study what the generator needs from retrieved pages through two requirements: Loud, making full use of visual token capacity, and Clear, refining the page so that its evidence becomes prominent. For Loud, increasing either the visual token budget or visual fidelity, the image resolution those tokens preserve, improves accuracy with the other held fixed, and full-page scaling outperforms repetition and tiling at matched budgets. For Clear, suppressing surrounding content improves accuracy without enlarging selected regions, and adding OCR of these regions to page images outperforms either input alone. We implement both as Loud and Clear (LoC), which combines higher-resolution pages with OCR from query-relevant regions without ground-truth annotations or additional training. LoC outperforms eight prior methods on SciEGQA, ViDoRe-v3, and MMLongBench-Doc, improving over the strongest, ColQwen3, by 8.88, 3.09, and 4.22 points with the same retriever and generator. It also outperforms its page-only variant under the same visual token budget. These results locate a bottleneck beyond retrieval: how the retrieved pages are given to the generator.

title: Does Zero-Edit Practice Support a Claim to Human Authorship?
abstract: This article examines whether meaningful human authorship can survive full post-generation delegation to a generative AI system: a condition in which a human originates a concept, directs and iterates on its generation, evaluates and selects a result, but performs no subsequent modification of the output. The author’s earlier article, cited in the references, proposed a five-dimension agency framework for evaluating Zero-Edit practice. The present article takes a different approach: it examines the authorship question through five external approaches (Deng; Anscomb; Fritz; Militsyna; Huang et al.), none of which was developed with full post-generation delegation as its central case. These approaches are not treated as equivalent tests: Anscomb supplies a theoretical analogy, while the others are assessed according to their distinct analytical aims. The analysis applies these approaches to the author’s own Zero-Edit practice as a boundary case, using primary sources rather than secondary summaries. It distinguishes creative agency, expressive control, and execution; engages two substantial counterarguments through first-person case evidence; and tests the practice against one of its own weaker instances, allowing that case to count against the thesis where warranted. The case does not establish authorship under any single framework. Under Deng’s approach, the conception is thin under Factor One, while Factor Two shows some iteration but does not establish the degree of control exercised over the generative process. The central finding is therefore that sufficient expressive control remains undemonstrated across these factors. Huang et al.’s standard reveals a separate evidentiary finding: without contemporaneous records of prompts, rejected outputs, and iteration, a Zero-Edit authorship claim cannot be demonstrated through process evidence and rests instead on retrospective self-report.

title: No Poker Face: Why AI Can't Keep the Answer to Itself
abstract: Preprint (v1.1) of “No Poker Face: Why AI Can’t Keep the Answer to Itself” by Vijay Suresh, with the full data and code release. Learners increasingly ask AI models to write practice questions. A practice question is only useful if answering it requires the knowledge it tests. This paper studies clue leakage: properties of a question, other than the tested knowledge, that let someone answer it. Following earlier work on fictional subjects, it uses invented subjects that no model can know, so any accuracy above chance by a solver without the study material is leakage. Main pre-registered study (168 seven-round study sessions, 11,760 questions, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol as writers): neither confirmatory hypothesis was supported. Writers did not make sets easier after heavy reported failure, and none declared a learner ready on an unsupported mastery claim (0/24 vs 0/24). But a solver with no study material answered about half of all questions correctly (chance 25%), and asking for harder questions made them longer and more guessable, not harder. Pre-registered confirmatory follow-up (112 sessions, two new invented subjects): difficulty requests raised no-material accuracy by +5.9 points (95% CI 1.9 to 9.5, one-sided p = 0.002). An instruction to make wrong options as long and specific as the correct one removed the “longest option is correct” cue (37.6% → 25.6%) but did not reduce leakage (+2.2 points, p = 0.95). Removing the visible cue does not remove the leak. A 28-session Gemini 3.1 Pro arm and a real learner’s exam-prep sessions (case study) show the same patterns. Pre-registrations: osf.io/uya5q (main), osf.io/93vpn (Addendum 1), osf.io/3z64e (Addendum 2). Code: github.com/vjgits/research-papers. The zip contains transcripts, item-level solver results, per-call cost ledgers, analysis outputs, independent recomputation scripts and a log of every AI error made while running the study. Human-coder validation will follow in v1.2.

title: YSP0Github/SeisY-Releases: SeisY v0.1.10
abstract: SeisY 0.1.10 更新说明 发布日期:2026-10-15 本版本为问题修复与稳定性增强版本,重点修复了部分用户安装 0.1.9 后无法启动的问题,并系统排查、消除了同类隐患。 一、关键修复:无 G 盘电脑启动崩溃 问题现象:部分用户安装 0.1.9 后首次启动即报错退出: Failed to execute script 'gui' due to unhandled exception: FileNotFoundError: [WinError 3] 系统找不到指定的路径。: 'G:\\' 根本原因:安装包内随包分发的 Config.ini 残留了开发机的工作目录配置(work_dir = G:\...)。程序启动时会自动创建该工作目录,当用户电脑上没有 G 盘时,os.makedirs 直接失败,程序在主界面出现前崩溃。 修复内容: 启动目录自动回退:配置中的工作目录若指向不存在的盘符(如 G:\、H:\),自动切换到用户主目录下的 SeisY_Projects 文件夹,并在启动后给出一次性提示,告知用户新的工作目录位置。 全路径校验:缓存目录、数据保存目录、Apollo 数据库目录、仪器响应文件等路径同样做盘符校验,无效时自动重建或清空,避免后续功能再因同类问题报错。 清理出厂配置:随包分发的 Config.ini 已移除所有开发机绝对路径,工作目录、缓存、数据库等均在首次启动时于用户目录下自动创建。 升级后工作目录默认为:C:\Users\<你的用户名>\SeisY_Projects,可在「配置 → 修改配置」中随时修改。 二、其他健壮性改进 Apollo 月震数据库:配置指向不存在盘符时,自动回退到用户目录下的 database,不再依赖开发机路径。 批量去异常 / 双库对比查看器:默认数据库路径改为用户主目录,不再写死 G:\SeisY_Project\...。 月球昼夜分布图、3D 地球、测试数据浏览等功能中的贴图与起始目录改为相对程序目录解析,不再依赖固定盘符。 新增 12 项回归测试(路径盘符防护),覆盖"缺失盘符启动""配置二次加载校验""出厂配置守护"等场景,防止该问题复发。 三、0.1.9 老用户临时解决办法(不升级也可) 若暂时无法升级,可手动删除安装目录下的配置文件后重启,程序会自动重建: C:\Users\<用户名>\AppData\Local\Programs\SeisY\_internal\seisy\Config.ini 直接安装 0.1.10 即可覆盖解决,无需手动处理。 校验信息 安装包:SeisY-0.1.10-Setup.exe(约 818 MB) SHA-256: 2C959BDE89087AB2B6E347F3763E632B2E14B9E81BEAF04F4D4074ACAFEABF4F 也可下载随附的 SeisY-0.1.10-SHA256.txt 核对。

title: Diagnosing Unconditional Migration in the Snow Ablation Optimizer Through Controlled Retention Strategies
abstract: The Snow Ablation Optimizer (SAO) uses ranked solutions to generate candidates but accepts every evaluated candidate, even when it degrades its source state. We examined whether this unconditional migration rule created a systematic risk for the individuals that contributed most to search progress. On 12 representative CEC2017 functions, current leaders produced a median 82.51% of generation-best improvements. title: Advanced Digital Signature Schemes for Blockchain Systems
abstract: It discusses about the advanced digital signature techniques that were specifically designed to cater to the needs of modern blockchain systems concerning scalability, privacy, and efficiency. Through the study of aggregate signatures, particularly the BLS scheme, the aim is to comprehend the process of reducing numerous signatures into one verifiable proof. Subsequently, the chapter touches on group signatures and ring signatures, revealing how they offer anonymity of the signers while ensuring accountability and verifiability. Blind signatures are scrutinized regarding their importance in privacy-centric applications like anonymous payments and voting. Proxy signatures are introduced as a technique for managing the signing authority delegation in decentralized workflows. For all the schemes, the reader is introduced to the mathematical intuition, security assumptions, and practical deployment issues. A comparative analysis at the end of the chapter facilitates the selection of the suitable signature schemes depending on the performance, privacy, and trust requirements in a given blockchain environment.

title: Patchwork: automated lattice surgery and space-time partitioning for real-time decoding
abstract: We introduce patchwork, a lattice-surgery compiler for arbitrary multi-qubit Pauli measurements on a prescribed narrow-corridor two-dimensional surface-code layout. Systematic geometric rules simplify stabilizer placement and gate scheduling, including for logical $Y$ measurements implemented using twist defects. We introduce measurement circuits and schedules that, together with protruding lobes of $Y$-extension patches, preserve the full effective code distance for all numerically tested code distances. To support parallel decoding, we develop a wavefront algorithm that partitions merged lattice-surgery patches into space-time commit, buffer, and cleanup regions. Simulations of three sequential multi-qubit Pauli measurements acting on ten logical qubits show that staged decoding achieves total failure probabilities close to those of monolithic decoding over the parameters tested. These methods provide an automated framework for fault-tolerant lattice surgery and a route toward scalable, real-time decoding.

title: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic $(L_0, L_1)$-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
abstract: We study the stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) complexity of finding $ε$-stationary points of $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth nonconvex functions. Under bounded-variance noise, existing analyses of normalized and clipped stochastic gradient descent (SGD) establish optimal dependence on $ε$ and $L_0$, but the jointly optimal dependence on $L_0$, $L_1$, and $ε$ remains unclear. We resolve this question for an unbiased SFO whose gradient noise has a $p$th central moment bounded by $σ^p$ for some $σ\geq 0$, where $p\in(1,2]$.Specifically, we establish an SFO lower bound of $Ω\big(\big(σ^{\frac{p}{p-1}}ε^{-\frac{p}{p-1}}+1\big) (L_0 Δε^{-2}+L_1Δε^{-1})\big)$, where $Δ>0$ is the initial optimality gap.This bound identifies an unavoidable contribution proportional to $L_1ε^{-1}Δ$. We also prove that mini-batch (smoothed) normalized SGD can attain a matching upper bound, thereby establishing the optimal SFO complexity.

title: "Do You Trust It... or Check It?": Exploring Children's Verification Behaviors in Game-Based Human-AI Collaboration
abstract: Children are increasingly interacting with AI agents in learning and problem-solving contexts, where AI suggestions may appear fluent, helpful, and socially engaging. However, children may not always be able to judge whether such suggestions are accurate, incomplete, or misleading. This paper presents a game-based human-AI collaboration probe designed to examine how children verify AI suggestions during task-based interaction. The system embeds AI suggestions within a biological knowledge reasoning game and compares three Agent interaction styles: partner-like, tool-like, and dual-state Agent. Instead of treating trust as a static post-task attitude, this study focuses on children's situated verification behaviors, including acceptance, evidence checking, questioning, revision, and continued AI use. A preliminary evaluation with children aged 8-10 combined interaction logs, post-task ratings, and semi-structured interviews. The findings suggest that Agent style shaped children's engagement and response pathways: partner-like interaction tended to support direct questioning, while tool-like interaction was more associated with evidence seeking. Children generally viewed AI as useful but fallible, and their questioning behaviors varied in reasoning depth. The study contributes design insights for supporting children's critical, reflective, and evidence-based use of AI in collaborative tasks.

title: Amora: Communication-Efficient Private Approximate Nearest Neighbors Search
abstract: Approximate nearest neighbors search (ANNS) over cloud-hosted vector databases raises a critical privacy concern: the query vector, which often encodes sensitive user intent, is exposed to the server. Private ANNS (PANNS) allows a client to retrieve nearest neighbors without revealing its query. The state-of-the-art single-server scheme, Pacmann (ICLR'25), achieves high accuracy via graph-based search with private information retrieval (PIR), but incurs substantial communication overhead because each PIR query retrieves only a single vertex. We present Amora, a communication-efficient PANNS system that applies SimplePIR to a partitioned graph index so that one PIR query is amortized over many vertices. To retrieve as much of the distance and neighbor information the search needs under a limited communication budget, Amora adopts a dual-PIR split layout with two heterogeneous PIR matrices that stay balanced in dimension: VecPIR retrieves inner products for an entire partition of vertices as their distance at once, while NbrPIR retrieves necessary neighbor lists at subgroup granularity for graph traversal. This layout shifts the cost model of PIR query from per-vertex to per-partition, which significantly reduces the communication overhead. To further improve efficiency by reducing the number of scans and query rounds in the PIR database, Amora introduces batch PIR to pack multiple queries into one matrix multiplication, centroid-based pruning to filter unpromising partitions, and TopCand exploration that seeds jump-style graph navigation with the closest vertices from each retrieved partition. We evaluate Amora on five datasets spanning 96 to 1024 dimensions and up to 10 million vectors. Compared to Pacmann, Amora reduces online communication by 93--99% while achieving higher search accuracy.
